Create a personal access token, or a deploy token with --repo

Create a token and show its secret once.

Without --repo this creates a PERSONAL ACCESS TOKEN, bound to your user, with
the scopes of --scope (repo:read, repo:write, repo:manage; repeat the flag or
separate with commas; default repo:read). repo:read also reads scan results.
It lives 365 days unless --expires-in is shorter.

With --repo &lt;name&gt; this creates a DEPLOY TOKEN, bound to that repository only,
for package clients. --username sets the username of the pair (the server
generates one when it is empty), --read-only limits it to pulls.
--scope does not apply to a deploy token.

The secret is shown once and cannot be read again. rp prints it on stdout only
when you pass --show-secret (the bare token, one line) or a structured output
(--output json|yaml, or --jq). Without one of them rp refuses before it creates
anything, so a token is never created and lost. Everything else rp prints goes
to stderr. The secret is never taken from a flag.

```
TOKEN=$(rp token create --name ci --scope repo:write --show-secret)
rp token create --name ci --repo libs --read-only --output json --jq .token
```

```
rp token create [flags]
```

## Options

```
      --expires-in string   Lifetime, for example 30d or 720h (at most 365d; default: the server's, 365 days)
      --name string         Name of the token (required, at most 80 characters)
      --read-only           Make a deploy token read-only
      --repo string         Create a deploy token for this repository (without it: a personal access token)
      --scope strings       Scopes of a personal access token: repo:read, repo:write, repo:manage (default repo:read)
      --show-secret         Print the secret on stdout (once); implied by a structured --output
      --username string     Username of a deploy token (default: generated by the server)
```
